issues.description: The problem statement contains conflicting information about the type used for the Farm.animals collection: the UML diagram declares animals as List<Animal>, while the textual Part 3 instructions require a Set implemented with a HashSet. The provided solution implements animals as a List/ArrayList, which follows the UML but contradicts the Part 3 textual requirement to use a HashSet. This ambiguity can confuse students about whether to use a List or a Set (and whether uniqueness must be enforced), and the solution does not match the textual specification.
issues.suggestedFix: Resolve the mismatch by choosing one collection type and updating all artifacts accordingly. Option A (preferred if uniqueness is intended): update the UML and the solution to use Set<Animal> and initialize it with new HashSet<>() in the Farm constructor; update any code/comments referencing List to Set. Option B (if ordering/duplicates are acceptable): update the textual Part 3 instructions to require a List (ArrayList) and remove references to HashSet. Ensure the template, problem text, UML, and solution are consistent with the chosen collection type.

issues.description: The problem statement requires that Farm's aggregation of animals is realized using a Set implemented with a HashSet, but the solution implementation uses a List (ArrayList). The template also does not declare the animals collection yet (TODO). This mismatched collection type (Set/HashSet vs List/ArrayList) creates a conceptual naming/implementation inconsistency that can confuse students about the expected data structure for Farm.animals.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the collection type consistent with the problem statement: declare Farm.animals as a Set<Animal> and initialize it with new HashSet<>() in both the template and solution (update imports and any code that relies on List-specific behavior). Alternatively, update the problem statement to accept List/ArrayList if Set semantics are not required.
